title: Add RAG scenario-generator CLI and compact authoring scripter
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Authoring high-fidelity RAG scenarios for local development and CI is time-consuming and brittle. This PR introduces a small, focused CLI (raggen) plus a compact 'authoring scripter' that scaffolds reproducible scenario templates, seeded corpora, and lightweight telemetry probes for local evaluation.

Goals: 1) lower onboarding friction for product engineers writing scenario-driven tests; 2) provide deterministic seed data and step assertions for e2e RAG smoke tests; 3) ship an example integration to the DevLoop devcontainer and CI smoke runner.

What this PR adds:
- raggen CLI (Python) with commands: init, seed, compile, run.
- A compact scenario DSL (rag.yml) that supports steps, tool stubs, expected assertions, and optional telemetry hooks.
- Authoring scripter utility that emits minimal runnable sandboxes (devcontainer/ and .ragci/) and a seeded JSONL corpus for offline indexers.
- A small test runner (pytest plugin) and a headless smoke runner that exercises tool-calling and structured-output contracts.
- Documentation and a one-page quickstart (docs/rag-scenario-generator.md) with examples and recommended telemetry probes.

Developer UX:
- raggen init --template=compact creates a pre-seeded workspace with a devcontainer, rag.yml, sample index (seed-corpus.jsonl), and example tool stubs under tools/
- raggen seed --count=50 populates the local index with deterministic, annotated records to make replayable runs trivial.
- raggen run --ci exercises the scenario in headless mode, emitting compact traces that map to our telemetry schema.

Example rag.yml snippet (generated by raggen init):
steps:
  - name: FindCompanyPolicy
    type: retrieval
    query: "employee expense policy reimbursement"
    expect:
      contains: ["reimbursement", "30 days"]
  - name: SummarizePolicy
    type: llm
    model: small-instruct
    tools:
      - name: policy_extractor
        contract: '{"input":"text","output":"json"}'

Why this is different: Instead of shipping a large sample app, raggen focuses on compact, reproducible authoring workflows that integrate into both local devcontainers and CI smoke suites. The seeded corpus and step assertions let teams iterate on prompt/contract changes with confidence and guardrails.

Related work: builds on ideas from ENG-1107 (scenario seeding) and the telemetry schema from ENG-2050.

Checklist:
- [x] raggen CLI implementation + unit tests
- [x] compact scenario DSL + parser
- [x] seeded corpus generator
- [x] pytest plugin + smoke runner
- [x] docs quickstart and examples
- [x] devcontainer integration
- [x] CI smoke job template

Notes for reviewers: The CLI is intentionally small (single-file entrypoint) to keep maintenance burden low. The seeded corpus uses a fixed RNG seed so outputs are deterministic. Telemetry hooks are opt-in via rag.yml to avoid accidental telemetry in customer examples. Please run the devcontainer quickstart and the headless smoke runner as part of review (instructions in docs/rag-scenario-generator.md).
